entries.capabilityHypothesis: Explicit holder binding and direct birth-claim predicates expose reusable core semantics.
knownLimitations: The private prototype has no supported product profile or release authority.
Its concrete birth schema is outside the core-only repository boundary.
entries.exitCriterion: Move schema-neutral holder-binding and predicate cases into conformance vectors, then delete the workspace and its catalog, target, and artifact references.
blockers: VC maintainer approval is required before deletion.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: Commitment-backed claims and hidden holder binding expose reusable privacy semantics.
knownLimitations: The private prototype has no supported product profile or release authority.
Its concrete birth schema is outside the core-only repository boundary.
entries.exitCriterion: Capture commitment and hidden-holder behavior in schema-neutral conformance vectors, then delete the workspace and all repository wiring.
blockers: VC maintainer approval is required before deletion.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: A minimal direct-claim family can demonstrate the public core construction surface.
knownLimitations: The current package contains a concrete family and generated contract surface.
The replacement fixture must not retain DID, transport, deployment, or product behavior.
entries.exitCriterion: Replace its useful construction evidence with the thin synthetic core-composition example, then delete this family workspace and aliases.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: A broad direct-claims shape can expose encoding and verifier-boundary defects.
knownLimitations: The broad synthetic schema is redundant once equivalent canonical vectors exist.
The package is private and has no release or interoperability claim.
entries.exitCriterion: Preserve distinct encoding and malformed-input cases as core vectors, then delete the package and dummy-claims targets.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: Mixed direct and commitment-backed claims test canonical claim representation.
knownLimitations: The private family is not a supported credential profile.
Its package-specific claim-mode matrix is not a core interoperability contract.
entries.exitCriterion: Keep the schema-neutral claim boundary in the core specification and marker types, then delete the package-specific family and tests.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: The passport family validates that an independently released family can consume only public VC core packages.
knownLimitations: The destination has not yet supplied immutable clean-consumer validation evidence to this ledger.
The local package remains a frozen duplicate until the handoff gate passes.
entries.exitCriterion: Record a destination revision that installs released core packages and passes its clean build, tests, and shared conformance vectors, then remove the local duplicate.
blockers: Destination-owner approval and immutable consumer evidence are required.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: An independently governed diploma family can consume canonical core objects and own its schema, circuits, artifacts, and release train.
knownLimitations: No accountable product owner or independent family repository is approved yet.
Current production-shaped evidence cannot remain in the core repository.
entries.exitCriterion: Assign a product owner and approved independent family repository, validate it through released core packages, then delete the local family workspace.
blockers: An accountable university credential product owner must be assigned.
The independent family repository must be approved before extraction.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: The age-gate flow provides application evidence for request binding, predicates, holder binding, replay handling, and optional status.
knownLimitations: The flow is product-shaped application evidence, not a core protocol or supported profile.
Destination validation through released packages has not yet been recorded.
entries.exitCriterion: Pass maintained age-gate scenarios in the destination through released core and family packages, retain only schema-neutral vectors here, then remove both local workspaces.
blockers: Destination-owner approval and passing destination CI are required.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: Shared BDD utilities support the current age-gate and university application scenarios.
knownLimitations: The utilities have no core consumer after application scenarios relocate.
They are application test infrastructure rather than VC semantics.
entries.exitCriterion: Remove the workspace after age-gate and university scenarios leave; destinations may independently implement their own test support.
blockers: Issues #542 and #544 must remove every in-repository BDD consumer first.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: One minimal synthetic example can prove public credential-model and credential-compact composition without becoming a product.
knownLimitations: The current deployable contract workspace is larger than the permitted fixture.
The survivor cannot claim DID, transport, deployment, interoperability, or production support.
entries.exitCriterion: Replace the workspace with one private, non-packable, protocol-independent synthetic example using only public core exports and synthetic data.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: The flow exposed integration requirements between generic status semantics and an OpenID-shaped application.
knownLimitations: OpenID and application orchestration are excluded by ADR-0016.
No external protocol owner has accepted this evidence.
entries.exitCriterion: Retain only protocol-independent status validity and failure vectors, then delete the OpenID evidence workspace and its targets; Git history remains the archive unless an external owner accepts it first.
blockers: Coordinate deletion with high-level protocol removal issue #536.

entries.capabilityHypothesis: The university flow provides application evidence for independently composed issuance, presentation, verification, and reporting.
knownLimitations: No accountable solution owner has accepted the flow in the destination repository.
Protocol, reporting, business policy, and BDD surfaces are excluded from core.
entries.exitCriterion: Assign a destination owner, validate maintained scenarios through released family and core packages, retain schema-neutral vectors here, then remove all four workspaces and university-specific infrastructure.
blockers: A destination solution owner and passing destination CI are required.
